Maria V: FYI ran a quick replay vs synthetic run on rtf-v2 this morning. p95 moves from 110ms -> 170ms when microbatch=8, p99 jumps more (220ms -> 420ms). Need thoughts on whether this is legit or an artifact of our generator.
Sanjay P: interesting — was the replay preserving original interarrival timing or did you flatten to constant QPS?
Maria V: replayed trace with original timestamps (headroom scaled to target qps). synthetic was constant-poisson. both used same kernel selection (fast-attn-v3) and same quant profile.
Tess: synthetic poisson tends to under-sample burst spacing, so it can suppress tail caused by convoying. replay preserves convoying but can also bias p99 if trace has rare catastrophic events. hybrid helps.
Kevin L: iirc we saw a kernel change (automatic selection) last week that prefers tiled-gemm for seq>512. could that flip interact badly with microbatch merging + KV misses? saw a 10% p99 uplift on region-3 during rollout.
Maria V: logs attached (snippet):
```
[2026-03-05T09:21:12Z] req=abc123 microbatch=8 kv_hits=0 kernel=tiled-gemm latency=412ms
[2026-03-05T09:21:12Z] req=abc124 microbatch=1 kv_hits=10 kernel=fast-attn-v3 latency=98ms
```
Sanjay P: that pattern screams cache-cold + kernel path divergence. tiled-gemm has different memory working set so when KV miss forces cache rebuild you hit bad path.
perf-bot: ALERT: regression detected on canary (p99 +34% vs baseline). Trace id: 2026-03-05-canary-7. See /perf/alerts/1759992222.
deploy-bot: Canary of tiled-gemm auto-select rolled back at 09:45 UTC due to latency regression.
Tess: measurement note — how are we computing cluster p99? pooled across hosts or average of per-host p99s? they can diverge. pooled gives correct user-experience but is noisier.
Maria V: pooled. also use reservoir sketches to merge quantiles across machines. i can push config for q-digest if folks want reproducible numbers.
Kevin L: another confound: microbatching changes timing of KV cache writes (when we flush/compact). With larger microbatch we observed delayed evictions that coincide with big requests -> spike. Need to instrument KV hit latency distribution.
Sanjay P: proposal: run three experiments — 1) replay preserving interarrivals, 2) synthetic poisson with same mean qps, 3) bursty synthetic (per-trace burst windows) — measure pooled p95/p99 + per-host 95/99 and hist tails. Also track kernel path counts and kv-hit-rate per-request.
Tess: +1. add a warmup phase for each run and report warm vs steady-state. include a small script to force KV warm (e.g., prefill prefix=recent 10k keys) so we can separate cold-cache regressions.
Maria V: putting together a plan. quick loadgen snippet for reproducibility:
```
loadgen --mode=replay --trace=/traces/customerA.log --scale=0.3 --warmup=300 --report=p95,p99,host_quantiles
loadgen --mode=synthetic --pattern=bursty --burstiness=0.2 --qps=200 --warmup=300
```
Kevin L: also capture kernel-selection telemetry: `kernel=fast-attn-v3|tiled-gemm` per span, and kv_hit_rate per request. we can correlate in a spark job.
Sanjay P: for aggregation, use merged t-digest for p95/p99 across hosts to avoid taking mean-of-p99s. will script this.
Maria V: ok i'll run two replays tomorrow (EU and US traces), baseline with microbatch=1, and runs with microbatch=4 and 8. will post results + small heatmap of kernel vs latency.
Tess: thanks — can we add a small A/B where we pin kernel=fast-attn-v3 even for seq>512 so we can isolate kernel impact?
Kevin L: yes. also try forcing kv-prefetcher on/off.
Maria V: cool. scheduling a 30min postmortem/workshop tomorrow 10:00 UTC to review results. tagging @Sanjay P @Tess @Kevin L. :calendar: :coffee:
Sanjay P: will join.
Tess: will be there.
perf-bot: Reminder: attach raw histograms to the issue so alerting thresholds can be tuned (avoid flapping).
Maria V: will attach everything. thanks all. :thumbsup:
